symbols.name: source length
symbols.meaning: The number of entries of the source vector $u$.
symbols.quote: Let $s$ and $t$ be the number of entries of the source and target vectors, with $\gcd(s,t)=1$ and $\theta=t/s-1$ the relative gap between them.

symbols.name: target length
symbols.meaning: The number of entries of the target vector $g$.
symbols.quote: Let $s$ and $t$ be the number of entries of the source and target vectors, with $\gcd(s,t)=1$ and $\theta=t/s-1$ the relative gap between them.

symbols.name: relative gap
symbols.meaning: The relative gap $t/s-1$ between the target and source lengths.
symbols.quote: Let $s$ and $t$ be the number of entries of the source and target vectors, with $\gcd(s,t)=1$ and $\theta=t/s-1$ the relative gap between them.

symbols.name: source vector
symbols.meaning: A vector of length $s$, the input of the maps $S$ and $N$.
symbols.quote: Let $u$ be a source vector of length $s$ and $g$ a target vector of length $t$.

symbols.name: target vector
symbols.meaning: A vector of length $t$, the input of the permutation $P_t$.
symbols.quote: Let $u$ be a source vector of length $s$ and $g$ a target vector of length $t$.

symbols.name: source position
symbols.meaning: A position in the source vector $u$, not an output index of the DFT.
symbols.quote: Here $j$ is a position in $u$ and $k$ a position in $g$, so they are not the output and input indices of the DFT page.

symbols.name: target position
symbols.meaning: A position in the target vector $g$, not an input index of the DFT.
symbols.quote: Here $j$ is a position in $u$ and $k$ a position in $g$, so they are not the output and input indices of the DFT page.

symbols.name: source transform
symbols.meaning: The normalized Fourier transform on length-$s$ vectors.
symbols.quote: Let $F_s$ be the normalized Fourier transform on length-$s$ vectors and $P_s$ the coordinate permutation $(P_s u)_j=u_{tj}$.

symbols.name: source permutation
symbols.meaning: The coordinate permutation of length-$s$ vectors with $(P_s u)_j=u_{tj}$.
symbols.quote: Let $F_s$ be the normalized Fourier transform on length-$s$ vectors and $P_s$ the coordinate permutation $(P_s u)_j=u_{tj}$.

symbols.name: target transform
symbols.meaning: The normalized Fourier transform on length-$t$ vectors.
symbols.quote: Let $F_t$ and $P_t$ be the transform and the permutation $(P_t g)_k=g_{-sk}$ on length-$t$ vectors.

symbols.name: target permutation
symbols.meaning: The coordinate permutation of length-$t$ vectors with $(P_t g)_k=g_{-sk}$.
symbols.quote: Let $F_t$ and $P_t$ be the transform and the permutation $(P_t g)_k=g_{-sk}$ on length-$t$ vectors.

symbols.name: gathering map
symbols.meaning: The Gaussian-weighted map from length-$s$ to length-$t$ vectors that gathers entries of $u$ near $sk/t$.
symbols.quote: $S$ gathers the entries of $u$ near $sk/t$, and $T$ spreads each $u_j$ over the targets near $tj/s$.

symbols.name: spreading map
symbols.meaning: The Gaussian-weighted map from length-$s$ to length-$t$ vectors that spreads each $u_j$ over targets near $tj/s$.
symbols.quote: $S$ gathers the entries of $u$ near $sk/t$, and $T$ spreads each $u_j$ over the targets near $tj/s$.

symbols.name: Gaussian width
symbols.meaning: The integer that sets the width of the Gaussian weights in $S$ and $T$.
symbols.quote: The integer $\alpha$ sets the width of the Gaussian weights, which are bell-shaped functions of $j$ that decay quickly away from their centres.

symbols.name: nearest target index
symbols.meaning: The integer nearest $tj/s$, with ties rounded up.
symbols.quote: For $0\le j<s$, let $\ell_j$ be the integer nearest $tj/s$, ties rounded up, and $\beta_j=tj/s-\ell_j$.

symbols.name: rounding offset
symbols.meaning: The offset $tj/s-\ell_j$ of $tj/s$ from its nearest integer.
symbols.quote: For $0\le j<s$, let $\ell_j$ be the integer nearest $tj/s$, ties rounded up, and $\beta_j=tj/s-\ell_j$.

symbols.name: summation index
symbols.meaning: An integer index summed over all of $\mathbb Z$ in the expansion of $Nu$.
symbols.quote: The same rule defines $\ell_h$ and $\beta_h$ for every integer $h$, which is the summation index used below.

symbols.name: coordinate selection
symbols.meaning: The map $(Cg)_j=g_{\ell_j}$ that selects, for each $j$, the entry of $g$ at $\ell_j$.
symbols.quote: Let $C$ select coordinates, $(Cg)_j=g_{\ell_j}$, let $D$ be the diagonal map $(Du)_j=e^{\pi\alpha^2\beta_j^2}u_j$, and set $N=CTD$, a map from length-$s$ to length-$s$ vectors.

symbols.name: diagonal map
symbols.meaning: The diagonal map scaling $u_j$ by $e^{\pi\alpha^2\beta_j^2}$.
symbols.quote: Let $C$ select coordinates, $(Cg)_j=g_{\ell_j}$, let $D$ be the diagonal map $(Du)_j=e^{\pi\alpha^2\beta_j^2}u_j$, and set $N=CTD$, a map from length-$s$ to length-$s$ vectors.

symbols.name: near-identity map
symbols.meaning: The map $CTD$ from length-$s$ to length-$s$ vectors, close to the identity.
symbols.quote: Let $C$ select coordinates, $(Cg)_j=g_{\ell_j}$, let $D$ be the diagonal map $(Du)_j=e^{\pi\alpha^2\beta_j^2}u_j$, and set $N=CTD$, a map from length-$s$ to length-$s$ vectors.

symbols.name: identity map
symbols.meaning: The identity map on length-$s$ vectors.
symbols.quote: Let $I$ be the identity map on length-$s$ vectors, so $N-I$ collects the remaining terms.

symbols.name: error map
symbols.meaning: The error $I-N$ between the identity and $N$.
symbols.quote: Write $E=I-N$ for the error, so $N=I-E$.

symbols.name: Neumann index
symbols.meaning: The summation index of the Neumann series, not the shifted index of the DFT page.
symbols.quote: The Neumann series is the operator version of the geometric series, $\sum_{r\ge0}E^r$, with $r$ its summation index.

symbols.name: last partial index
symbols.meaning: The last index of a partial Neumann sum.
symbols.quote: Let $R$ be the last index of a partial sum $\sum_{r=0}^{R}E^r$.

symbols.name: precision parameter
symbols.meaning: An integer precision parameter, greater than 100.
symbols.quote: Here $p>100$ is an integer precision parameter, not the first integer of the radix-digit page, and the estimate applies when $\alpha$ is an integer with $2\le\alpha<p$, $\gcd(s,t)=1$ and $\theta>p/\alpha^4$.

symbols.name: retained-permutation map
symbols.meaning: The linear map $DN^{-1}C$ in the identity $P_sF_s=BP_tF_tS$.
symbols.quote: Multiplying on the left by $N^{-1}$ and then by $D$ gives $P_sF_s=DN^{-1}C\,P_tF_tS$, which has the form $P_sF_s=BP_tF_tS$ with $B=DN^{-1}C$ a linear map.

relations.quote: Gaussian resampling replaces a [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) of arbitrary length by transforms whose axis lengths are powers of two, using Gaussian weights to move between the two sets of frequencies.
It replaces the transforms for the [radix-digit convolution](radix-digit-convolution.md) of two integers by such transforms.
The error $E$ is measured in the [operator norm](operator-norm.md) for the maximum-modulus vector norm, and $\|E\|=\|N-I\|$.
